title: Writ Petition — Certiorari (Article 226/32)
description: Writ of certiorari to quash an order, decision, or proceeding of an inferior court, tribunal, or quasi-judicial authority for want or excess of jurisdiction, violation of natural justice, or error of law apparent on the face of the record.

additional_respondents.label: Additional Respondents (private parties to original proceedings)

options: Error of law apparent on face of record
ground_invoked.label: Grounds for Certiorari

natural_justice_breach.label: Specific NJP breach (no hearing, biased decision-maker, etc.)

error_on_face.label: Error of law apparent on record (specify legal provision misapplied)

jurisdictional_defect.label: Jurisdictional defect (lack of subject-matter / pecuniary / territorial jurisdiction)

relief_sought.label: Specific relief — quash which order, what consequential direction

mandatory_clauses: Cause title with petitioner v. authority (whose order impugned) + private respondents
Impugned order — date, authority, case number, prayer to quash
Grounds — jurisdictional error / NJP / error on face / fraud
If NJP: specific breach (no notice, no hearing, biased forum, no opportunity to cross-examine)
If error on face: quote the impugned order passage and the legal provision misapplied
Limitation — writ filed within reasonable time (no rigid period, but unexplained delay fatal)
Prayer to issue writ of certiorari quashing impugned order with consequential directions
Annexure: certified copy of impugned order

prompt_context.system_role: You are drafting a Writ of Certiorari under Article 226/32. Certiorari issues to quash an order of an inferior tribunal/court/quasi-judicial authority on these grounds only: (1) want or excess of jurisdiction (including jurisdictional fact wrongly assumed), (2) violation of principles of natural justice (audi alteram partem, nemo judex in causa sua), (3) error of law apparent on the face of the record (must be self-evident, not requiring long argument), (4) fraud on the court. Cite Hari Vishnu Kamath v. Ahmad Ishaque AIR 1955 SC 233 (classical grounds), Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai (2003) 6 SCC 675 (HC certiorari over civil courts and tribunals). Certiorari does NOT lie against purely administrative orders; the body must exercise judicial or quasi-judicial functions.
style_notes: Annex certified copy of impugned order — pleading must refer to it as Annexure P-1
For 'error on face' ground — quote the offending passage verbatim and identify the legal error
For NJP — be specific about which limb breached (notice, hearing, bias, reasoned order)
Frame prayer as 'issue a writ of certiorari or any other appropriate writ, order or direction quashing the impugned order dated ___ passed by ___ in ___'

relevantActs.notes: Article 227 supervisory jurisdiction often clubbed with certiorari

relevantActs.act: Statute under which impugned order was passed
relevantActs.notes: To show authority acted in judicial/quasi-judicial capacity

key_precedents.case: Hari Vishnu Kamath v. Ahmad Ishaque
key_precedents.principle: Classical four grounds for certiorari: jurisdictional defect, NJP breach, error on face, fraud

key_precedents.case: Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai
key_precedents.principle: HC can issue certiorari to civil courts and tribunals subordinate to it
Error of law apparent on face — must be self-evident, not requiring lengthy argument
Scope and conditions for certiorari under Article 226
Certiorari against judicial orders of civil courts — overruled portion of Surya Dev Rai; Article 227 is route

filing_checklist: Memo of writ petition with index, synopsis, list of dates
Affidavit in support sworn before Oath Commissioner
Certified copy of impugned order (Annexure P-1) — mandatory
Copy of original proceedings/pleadings relevant to ground
If NJP ground: notice records, hearing records (or absence thereof)
Court fee per State HC Rules / SC Rules
Service copies for all respondents (authority + private parties)
Compliance with HC Rules of relevant State
Caveat search (private respondents likely to file caveat)

validation_rules.rule: At least one ground_invoked must be selected
If ground includes 'Violation of natural justice', natural_justice_breach must be filled
If ground includes 'Error of law apparent', error_on_face must be filled
Annexure of certified copy of impugned order is mandatory — flag if missing
Delay > 90 days from impugned order requires delay condonation pleading
Certiorari does not lie against purely administrative/legislative action — flag if pleading suggests this
